metadata.description: Skills for people who use AI a couple of times a week and do not live in a terminal. The general marketplace, and the one taught in the workshops.

plugins.name: setup
plugins.description: Runs once. Gets you from "I installed this" to "it knows who I am, and something runs tomorrow morning without me." Finds what it can, asks only what it cannot, shows you the whole suggestion, and writes the files every other skill reads. Its check skill tells you at any time which skills can run and which are blocked by which file.

plugins.name: writing
plugins.description: Four skills for work that already exists: put your voice back into generated text, catch the habits that mean nobody edited it, read a draft as the specific person who will push back, and reorder an answer so the reader knows what to do. Nothing here writes from scratch, sends, or publishes.

plugins.name: growth
plugins.description: The one that judges how you worked, not what you produced. Compares your week against the priorities you confirmed, ranks what is in front of you against them, keeps a running record of what actually went well in your own words, and gives feedback against a standard you set. Needs the files setup writes, and time-spent needs a configured calendar; source-based runs open by naming the evidence and the dates they actually read. Nothing here writes except the wins record, and only with your yes.

plugins.name: daily-hq
plugins.description: The day, run for you. A morning brief that ranks today against what changed and caps itself at seven items, a catch-up for when you were away that leads with what still needs you, the questions nobody ever answered, your mail and chat sorted by what needs you without touching anything, and a handover draft for before you go away. Needs the files setup writes and at least one configured source; every run names what it read, what it could not check, and the dates it covered. Nothing here sends anything, and nothing writes except the plugin's own snapshot, suppression and handover-pool files in your project folder.

plugins.name: learning
plugins.description: Three skills that compare you and your asks against the outside world: a cited brief on any topic, kept as a Word document and rerun on request; what strong looks like in your role right now against what you said you are working on; and the better shape for the thing you are about to ask for. The cited products need live web access and stop without it. Its triggers are lines in the project instructions, so a project set up before learning was installed has none until a skill hands over the paste.
